unverified: All 84 claims were found by the checker; nothing was dropped.

Release years: the compilations do not say whether each track is the singer's original 78 or a later re-recording, so every release year is null. The written year is the year the Spanish Wikipedia list gives for the song's première, not a recording date.
Lola Flores, A tu vera: the Lola Flores page dates it 1962, the Copla andaluza list 1964; year left null.
Peak 1933-1960 is a judgement from the dated songs and from 'flourished in the 1930s and 1940s' / 'A partir de 1950 ... cine musical' / 'En los años 1960 se vio desplazada'; no source states a peak.
Origin in Seville is a judgement (Sevillian writers and stars, the name 'copla andaluza'); no source names a birthplace for the genre. Madrid's theatres are an equal candidate.

Later presence in Mexico rests on one fact (Lola Flores filming three films there in 1955). Argentina (Imperio Argentina; a Wikipedia category 'Cantantes de coplas de Argentina') and Cuba (Juanita Reina in Havana 1957) were seen but are too thin for presence lines.
España cañí near: the 1995 year is the album's release date on the iTunes record, not quoted.
